findings.title: BYOD CLAIMS TEXAS HHSC, 2M RESIDENTS
findings.comment: Same day, same gang: Medicaid and SNAP data on two million Texans claimed while the agency whistles like it hears naught. Two flags planted in one afternoon, arrr.

findings.title: N0N DUMPS 830M EXPEDIA LOYALTY ROWS
findings.comment: 830 million loyalty rows, credential tokens, tokens to 20k private repos, all stamped NOT PAID — EXPOSED. Expedia's silence be louder than any broadside.

findings.title: N0N LEAKS VERTEX PRESCRIBER AND DEA DATA
findings.comment: 248k named prescribers and 237k DEA registration numbers set adrift after no coin crossed the deck. Premium phishing bait for the next voyage.

findings.title: SCARLETT LISTS RIDGECREST HOSPITAL
findings.comment: Third hospital on this crew's ledger since October. Regional ERs be the new doubloons and Scarlett's chest fills weekly, matey.

findings.title: HYFLOCK LEAKS CAMEROON DEFENSE TROOP DATA
findings.comment: Ministry of Defense troop data dumped on the dock. After Ecuador's police, this scrappy upstart collects uniforms like trophies.

findings.title: SILENT RANSOM LISTS NJ LAW FIRM WILENTZ
findings.comment: The vishing corsairs who once walked into law offices now list Wilentz, Goldman & Spitzer — a century of client secrets in one hull, no statement from the deck.

findings.title: PANDACLOUD SHILLS HOTMAIL HITS ON NIFLHEIM FORUM
findings.comment: PandaCloud hawks "Fresh HOTMAIL/MIX HITS" mail:pass pairs on niflheim.world, no samples, no prices, just a Telegram funnel where the real swindle happens below decks.

findings.title: MEGACLOUD PAYWALLS 95K MAILBOX CREDENTIALS ON NULEDBB
findings.comment: Tenured scallywag MegaCloud locks "95K Full Valid Mail Acccess MIX 08.11" behind forum credits; corporate mailboxes be the treasure, resold straight to BEC an' access brokers.

findings.title: DBHUNTER LISTINGS SAUDI CONTRACTOR, 54 IN 30 DAYS
findings.comment: DBHunter lists Cleveland Bridge with scanned government IDs an' source code, zero proof as usual; 54 listings in a month, this broker be flyin' a false flag for sport.

findings.title: N0N CHURNS OUT ANONYMIZED VICTIM #180 ON LEAK SITE
findings.comment: N0n posts "Company #180" with no name, no proof, no ransom figure, 116 listings in two months; extortion theater where the poster be hopin' fear outsells evidence.

findings.title: CHROME 157 FIXES EIGHTH EXPLOITED ZERO-DAY OF 2026
findings.comment: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free in XML, already sailin' the wild among nine fixes in 157.0.8103.50. Roll the update out before some scallywag's crafted XML boards yer fleet.

findings.title: OPENCTI 7.261109.0 SHIPS QUERY AN' TASK FIXES
findings.comment: Filigran plugs sluggish scoped-search filters an' runaway background tasks, so yer threat intel galleon rows a touch less like it's takin' on water. Update at yer leisure fer once, no cannon fire required.

findings.title: OPENAI INSIDER BUGGER PLEADS NOT GUILTY
findings.comment: Abdulrahman Alfozan denies planting a hidden recorder in an exec boardroom on Nov 6; the scallywag allegedly used chatbots to plan the caper, and no one's named his employer's flag yet.

findings.title: ESET NAMES SLIPPYNUNCHUCKS, SOGOU KEYBOARD BACKDOORED
findings.comment: China-aligned spooks hijacked DNS on a popular Chinese keyboard app to plant DarkVigil malware on victims abroad; yer typing software be a spy ship now, arrr.

findings.title: APT29 WATERING HOLES HARVEST MOBILE BOOTY
findings.comment: Cozy Bear poisoned legit sites across the US, Ukraine and Bulgaria, and even supply-chained a Ukrainian SEO tracker, to plunder iPhones and Androids with n-day exploits; no zero-days needed, just lazy patchers.

findings.title: CPGUARD UPDATE CHANNEL POISONED, 2,946 SERVERS HIT
findings.comment: OpsShield's own auto-update channel served a backdoor and password-harvesting script to nearly 3,000 Linux servers starting Nov 2; the scoundrels used stolen credentials, no cannon broadside required.

findings.title: STORM-0940 ARTEX AGENTS HUNT EXPOSED SECRETS
findings.comment: Nation-state-linked Storm-0940 set AI agents loose on GitHub to sniff out secrets and raid Azure Key Vaults, moving from discovery to plunder in five minutes flat; the robots be doing the pillagin' now.

findings.title: BITTER APT LURES SOUTH ASIA WITH FAKE INVITATIONS
findings.comment: BITTER APT sails into South Asian government and energy targets with counterfeit diplomatic lures delivering its PapRAT backdoor in Rust and C++; the bilge rats even named their malware after a pest, fittingly.

findings.title: GPUSTACK AUTH BYPASS HITS KEV
findings.comment: Trusting loopback traffic granted unauthenticated admin access; a forged header could seize the helm, mint API keys and steer workers into code execution.

findings.title: FREESWITCH SIP COMMAND INJECTION EXPLOITED
findings.comment: A crafted SIP MESSAGE can select the API chat protocol and run daemon commands—because apparently telephony needed an unauthenticated command hatch.

findings.title: OPENSSH PASSWORD BYPASS ENTERS KEV
findings.comment: Attackers are probing musl-based, PAM-less SSH servers where an absurdly long password may unlock disabled accounts; Alpine captains should patch to 10.6p2.

findings.title: ASPERA AUTHORIZATION FLAW EXPLOITED
findings.comment: IBM Aspera Faspex joined KEV for incorrect authorization, proving once again that “authorised user” need not mean “authorised action.”
